items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: With the Improvisational Arts Quintet, that’s the group I play with Kidd and Alvin Fielder

ctx.x: It is very strong man, yeah. ‘Cause I was telling some of the students today that most everyone in New Orleans’ family, there’s somebody who plays music. Say for instance like Kidd Jordan, he’s here today with the New Orleans Jazz Camp, he has a son who plays flute, a son who plays trumpet, a daughter who plays the violin and another daughter who sings. And his other three kids, they have something to do with music but you know, they don’t play. The Jordan Family. And the kids married into the family called the…
Did the musician’s union have much to do with the day-to-day music that was going on in New Orleans during your career?

items.title: Kidd Jordan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 24, 2006
items.q: So it’s hard, see ‘cause Clyde and all of them came up under me.

ctx.x: Just physically to pull that off.

That’s right. And him being ill man. I mean that was a hell of a feat. That’s right. But you know what? Now Clyde told you about a saxophone player named Alvin Thomas. We played a gig with Alvin Thomas and we didn’t know he had cancer. And he told me, he said, man I was up at the thing and he was playing so much at a jazz festival and he said he was going over.
